title: for Loops: Repeating with a Counter
learningObjectives: Identify initialization, condition, and update in a for loop.
Explain the execution order of a for loop header and body.
Trace a for loop to predict output and iteration count.
Write a for loop over a defined counter range.
Choose boundaries carefully to avoid off-by-one errors.

understand.concept: A for loop combines counter initialization, a condition check, and an update in one header. Initialization runs once. The condition is checked before each iteration, and the update runs after the body before the next condition check.
understand.whyItMatters: Keeping the counter setup, stopping rule, and step together makes counter-based repetition easier to read and review. It makes the intended range visible.
understand.analogy: A numbered lap plan: set the counter, check whether planned laps remain, complete a lap, then advance the counter.
understand.analogyLimit: This is a typical counter pattern. A for loop can use different expressions and is not limited to simple counting.

explain.narrative: The for header has three parts separated by semicolons: initialization, condition, and update. Initialization executes once. Before each iteration, the condition is evaluated; if true, the body executes. After the body, the update runs and control returns to the condition. If the condition is false, execution continues after the loop. Boundary choices such as < versus <= affect iteration count.

examples.title: Count from 1 through 4
examples.explanation: i starts at 1, the condition includes 4, and i increases after each body run.

examples.title: Start at zero
Count down
examples.explanation: The counter decreases, and the loop ends after n becomes 0.

examples.title: Skip by two
examples.explanation: The update adds 2 each iteration, printing even values in this range.

commonMistakes: Using < when the final boundary should be included, or <= when it should be excluded.
Starting at the wrong counter value for a zero-based range.
Forgetting or reversing the update so the counter does not approach termination.
Assuming the update happens before the body; it happens after the body.
Changing the counter inside the body as well as the header and unintentionally skipping values.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Print five stars as numbered lines
guidedTask.instructions: Use a for loop to print the numbers 1 through 5, each followed by a star symbol.
steps: Set a condition that allows the counter through 5.
Print the counter and a star.
Increment the counter by one in the header.
Trace when the condition becomes false.

independentTask.title: Independent: Build a countdown
independentTask.instructions: Write a for loop that prints 10, 8, 6, 4, and 2, then prints Finished after the loop.
requirements: Use a condition that stops after printing 2.
Decrease the counter by 2 per iteration.
Keep the final message outside the loop.
Explain initialization, condition, and update parts of the header.

hints: Initialization happens once, before the first condition check.
The condition is checked before each body execution.
The update happens after the body finishes.
Choose <= or < based on whether the final boundary should be included.
Use a decreasing counter and >= for a countdown range.
Trace counter values to confirm the exact number of iterations.

questions.prompt: Which part of a for loop header runs only once at the beginning?
questions.explanation: Initialization runs once before the first condition check.

questions.prompt: When does the update expression run in a standard for loop?
options: Only when the condition is false
questions.explanation: The body runs, then update occurs before the next condition check.

questions.prompt: What values are allowed if i starts at 0, increases by 1, and the condition is i < 5?
questions.explanation: The condition excludes 5, allowing i values 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4.

questions.prompt: Which header counts down from 4 to 1?
questions.explanation: The counter begins at 4, checks n >= 1, and decreases.

questions.prompt: What is an off-by-one error in a loop?
options: A range that runs one iteration too many or too few
A syntax error caused only by missing braces
A loop that always runs exactly once
questions.answer: A range that runs one iteration too many or too few
questions.explanation: Wrong starting values or boundary operators can alter iteration count by one.
